title: Session-aware cohort sculpting and pin lab notes
content:
Purpose:
- quick scratchpad for a canary that is session-aware (sticky clients) and uses tiered cohort sculpting + conservative pinning rules.
- capture playbook, checks, quick commands, and open questions — for Naomi + on-call handoff.

Context / motivation:
- We saw 2 incidents where per-request canaries introduced token-cost variance and cold-KV latency for long-lived sessions.
- Customers with sticky sessions (websocket / long polling) experience spikes when a subset of requests hit a new model variant mid-session.
- Want an approach that: avoids mid-session flips, reduces cold-starts for cohorts, keeps rollback simple.

Assumptions:
- client sessions are identifiable via client_session_id header (SDK).
- router supports per-session affinity + per-tenant fraction.
- we can pin session -> model variant mapping for up to 24h in redis (fast key-value).
- fallback variants exist: vX-quantized (fast), vX-pruned (cheaper), vY-stable (older but resilient).

High-level plan (steps):
1) PREP: bake model on staging with KV priming data + synthetic traffic that mirrors session lengths. verify p95/p99 baselines. (owner: Eli)
2) SHADOW: route 0% live traffic but mirror 5% of sessions to canary runtime to collect stateful metrics (cache-miss ratio, first-token latency per-session). (owner: Naomi)
3) COHORT CREATE: define cohorts by session-duration bucket and client-tier (free, paid-silver, paid-gold). (see table below)
4) SOFT PIN: for sessions that qualify, set session pin TTL=6h and start a slow ramp from 0.5% -> 5% -> 15%.
5) MONITOR: hold each step for 30m min and evaluate metrics.
6) GRADUAL WIDEN: increase only if thresholds met.
7) PIN DECIDE: after 24h of stable metrics, increase pin TTL to 24h for low-risk cohorts; leave short sessions at 6h.
8) FALLBACKS: automatic downgrade to vX-quantized on latency SLO breaches; full rollback to vY-stable on error-rate spikes.

Cohort definitions (quick):
- short-session (<60s): primarily idempotent queries, low KV demands. low-risk. start here.
- medium-session (60s-20m): likely stateful chat, moderate KV. medium-risk.
- long-session (>20m): high state, KV heavy, high risk for mid-flip. holdback to later waves.
- client-tier overrides: paid-gold get earlier ramp (but allow opt-out).

Safety thresholds (fast checks):
- p95 latency change <= +25% absolute vs baseline for cohort
- p99 latency change <= +40% absolute vs baseline
- error-rate (5xx or model-runtime failures) delta <= +0.5% absolute
- model divergence score (eval harness on sample prompts) no more than 3% regression on golden set
- token-cost/unit should not exceed baseline by >10% for free-tier cohorts

Prometheus / dashboards to watch (short list):
- runtime.first_token_latency.p50/p95/p99 per-cohort
- kv.cache_miss_rate per-session-duration-bucket
- inference.errors.rate per-tenant
- token_count.per_request and cost_estimate.per_minute
- model_eval.quality_regressions (nightly golden-run)
- router.routing_decision_breakdown (fraction pinned vs floating)

Quick commands (scratch):
- curl to simulate pinned session (replace):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${DEV_TOKEN}' -H 'client_session_id: test-pin-123' -d '{"model":"canary-v2","input":"hi"}'
- redis set (approx): redis-cli SETEX session:pin:test-pin-123 21600 "canary-v2"
- rollback script (simple): ./scripts/traffic-sweep --cohort=short-session --set-variant=vY-stable --force

Warmup patterns tried / notes:
- synthetic warm requests keyed by representative prompt shapes worked for stateless models but didn't prime KV.
- per-session KV prefill (run requests that exercise common system prompts and long history) reduced first-token p95 by ~120ms in staging.
- warmup cost tradeoff: 1 warmup request per session amortized is often cheaper than repeated cold misses across many tokens.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- sustained error-rate above threshold for 10m (after filtering noise).
- sudden p99 spike > 2x baseline sustained 5m.
- spike in token-cost per-min exceeding forecast +20% (billing alert).
- negative customer complaints flagged by CS triage channel.

Post-deploy checklist (first 3 hours):
- confirm session pin keys are being set (sample redis keys)
- verify router logs show expected pinned fraction per-cohort
- check top-10 clients by request rate for abnormalities
- run golden prompt set against canary and baseline, compare outputs in diff tool
- inform on-call + cs (Slack #deploy-watch) if moving to next ramp step

Open questions / TODOs:
- how long should we keep session pin TTL for background offline clients? (short TTL reduces cross-session memory but could re-expose to variant flips)
- need a quick flag to opt individual tenants out of pinning (legal / A/B restrictions).
- test: effect of pinning on multi-region clients — does client affinity break? (ticket: JIRA-REL-634)
- add synthetic KV prefill runner in CI that mirrors top-50 user sessions (owner: Ravi)

Notes to self / quick heuristics:
- when in doubt, favor lower-fraction and longer observation windows for long-session cohorts.
- prioritize decreasing friction for paid tiers but keep strict safety thresholds.
- keep telemetry lightweight: prefer sampling by session id, not per-request on high-rate clients.

References / anchors:
- previous priming notes: confluence:release/priming-experiments (see synthetic vs KV prefill results)
- PR for router affinity: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/871
- link to staging run logs: s3://redwood-deploys/staging/session-prime/2025-11-18/

End of scratchpad — will tidy later for runbook.
